;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**A suicide bomber kills two American troops near the [[Kandahar International Airport]] in [[Afghanistan]]. The [[Taliban insurgency]] claims responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attack-nato-idUSKBN1AI14S (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*[[List of British consorts|British royal consorts]]
**[[Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh]], retires from public appearances at the age of 96, after having completed 22,219 solo engagements since 1952. [http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-08-03/prince-philip-queen-elizabeth-royal-husband-retires/8769254 (ABC News (Australia))]

;Business and economy
*[[Affirmative action in the United States]]	
**The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] announces internally that it is to start investigating colleges which have admissions policies that are seen as unfair to [[Asian Americans]]. [http://www.newsweek.com/affirmative-action-college-admissions-explained-645482 (''Newsweek'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/08/01/us/politics/trump-affirmative-action-universities.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Floods in the United States: 2001–present|Floods in the United States]]
**Several streets in [[Miami]] and [[Miami Beach]] are underwater after [[2017 Atlantic hurricane season#Tropical Storm Emily|Tropical Depression Emily]] causes 102 to 178 millimetres of rain overnight. [http://www.cnn.com/2017/08/02/us/miami-severe-flooding/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Minnehaha Academy#2017 gas explosion|Minnehaha Academy gas explosion]]
**A natural gas explosion at college prep school [[Minnehaha Academy]] in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]], kills two staff members. Another nine people were injured, seven of whom are hospitalized, three in critical and four in serious condition. [https://apnews.com/f0a281ba42724049ab7a5c16401fa90e/1-dead,-1-missing-after-explosion-at-Minneapolis-school (AP)] [http://www.cbsnews.com/news/minneapolis-school-explosion-collapses-building/ (CBS News)]

;Health and medicine 
*[[Genome editing|Gene editing]]
**Teams of [[United States]]-based researchers, composed of American, [[China|Chinese]] and [[South Korea]]n scientists, successfully [[genome editing|edit]] a piece of faulty [[DNA]] that causes a deadly form of [[Cardiovascular disease|heart disease]] from [[cell (biology)|cells]] in [[human]] [[embryo]]s.  [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-40802147 (BBC)] [http://www.cnn.com/2017/08/02/health/crispr-human-embryos-gene-editing-study/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.sciencenews.org/article/crispr-gene-editing-human-embryos (''Science News Magazine'')] [https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/embryo-gene-editing-experiment-reignites-ethical-debate/ (''Scientific American'')]

;International relations
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States]] [[Donald Trump]] signs the [[Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act]]. [[Prime Minister of Russia]] [[Dmitry Medvedev]] calls it a "trade war". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-russia-idUSKBN1AI1Y4 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Impeachment in the Philippines]]
**Two impeachment complaints are filed in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house of the Philippine Congress]] against [[Supreme Court of the Philippines|Supreme Court]] [[Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Philippines|Chief Justice]] [[Maria Lourdes Sereno]]. [http://news.abs-cbn.com/news/08/02/17/impeachment-raps-filed-vs-chief-justice-sereno (ABS-CBN News)] [http://www.manilastandard.net/news/national/243179/cj-sereno-faces-impeachment-raps.html (''Manila Standard'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Papua New Guinean general election, 2017]]
**The [[parliament]] of [[Papua New Guinea]] [[Incumbent|re-elects]] [[Peter O'Neill]] as [[Prime Minister]], ending a chaotic election campaign marred by violence, which analysts fear may continue amid widespread voter unrest. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-papua-election-idUSKBN1AI0MF?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Venezuelan Constitutional Assembly election, 2017]]
**At a news briefing in [[London]], the CEO of [[Smartmatic]],  the Venezuelan-owned multinational company that provided the [[Electronic voting|election system]] used in  Sunday's election, says the number of those participating in the poll was tampered with, off by at least one million. [https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2017/08/02/541129956/venezuelan-poll-tampered-with-says-voting-system-company (NPR)]
*[[Immigration policy of the first Donald Trump administration|Immigration policy of Donald Trump]]
**[[United States]] President [[Donald Trump]], together with Senators [[Tom Cotton]] and [[David Perdue]], unveils the [[Reforming American Immigration for Strong Employment Act|RAISE Act]], a plan that would, if passed, reduce [[immigration to the United States|legal immigration to the U.S.]] by half each year, and implement a "merit-based system" prioritizing skilled workers, instead of the current family-based [[chain migration]] system. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/post-politics/wp/2017/08/02/trump-gop-senators-to-introduce-bill-to-slash-legal-immigration-levels/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.npr.org/2017/08/02/541104795/trump-to-unveil-legislation-limiting-legal-immigration (NPR)]

;Science and technology
*[[Effects of global warming on South Asia]]
**New research suggests that large parts of [[South Asia|Southern]] [[Southeast Asia|Asia]] may be uninhabitable by 2100 due to levels of [[humidity]] dangerous to humans. [http://news.nationalgeographic.com/2017/08/south-asia-heat-waves-temperature-rise-global-warming-climate-change/ (''National Geographic'')]
